# Two-year legal guarantee 

If you buy something for private use from a European trader, you are entitled to a two-year legal guarantee (European Directive 2019/771).Your seller has sole responsibility for providing this guarantee, i.e. they cannot simply refer you to the manufacturer. If the seller refuses to take responsibility, he must prove that you caused the problem (e.g. due to incorrect use or non-compliance with the maintenance instructions).

## Which term is applicable for which product?

The 2-year statutory guarantee applies to any new tangible items (e.g. a car, TV and/or smart phone) you purchase from a European trader in an individual capacity (i.e. not as part of your professional activities).

## Good to know 

In some countries, e.g. in the Netherlands, the legal guarantee is not always 2 years but depends on the expected lifespan of the product (e.g. a refrigerator has a longer lifespan than 2 years). After the first year, you must prove that you did not cause the problem.

The 2-year legal guarantee also applies to second-hand goods. The term can be reduced to 1 year, e.g. in Belgium and Germany. In France, second-hand goods have a legal guarantee of 2 years, but during the second year you must prove that you did not cause the problem.

title: Flight delays: How to claim compensation - BBC
highlights:
Under UK law, passengers may be entitled to compensation if a flight arrives at its destination more than three hours late and the airline is responsible for the delay.

The arrival time matters, not the departure time. If a flight leaves more than three hours late but arrives two hours and 45 minutes late, it will not meet the three-hour threshold.

The delay also needs to be the airline's fault. Technical faults and airline staff issues may be covered, but passengers are not usually entitled to compensation for disruption outside the airline's control, such as extreme weather or air traffic control restrictions.

The rules apply to flights departing from a UK airport, and to flights arriving in the UK on a UK or EU airline.

## How much could you get?

Compensation depends on the distance of the flight and how late you arrive.

- For flights of less than 1,500km, compensation is £220.

If your flight is delayed for long enough, the airline has a duty of care.

This can include meals, refreshments and a way to communicate, such as phone calls or emails.

If the delay means you have to stay overnight, the airline should arrange accommodation and transport between the airport and hotel.

The point at which this support starts depends on the length and distance of the flight, but passengers can be entitled to care during delays even if they are not entitled to compensation.
